goal: Transform Python pure-lookup engine into a native binary (Rust/C) with opaque external interface, read-only shared tables, and zero GPU dependency.
design_principles: Tables are READ-ONLY after build — memory-map them, share across processes
Hot paths are pure integer — direct C/Rust translation, no float
External interface is MINIMAL and OPAQUE — hide the kitchen
Each processor gets its own copy of tables — no contention, linear scaling
Binary is self-contained — tables embedded as data segment or loaded from file

phases.name: Binary Table Format — Replace Pickle
phases.description: Replace pickle cache with a flat binary format that can be memory-mapped by native code. The tables are the core — they must be portable.

tasks.detail: Header: magic 'PTBL', version, max_coord, table offsets. Then raw int32 arrays for _P, _S, _D, _SP, _prox. No Python objects, no dicts.
tasks.acceptance: Format spec document, all tables serialized to binary

tasks.detail: PtTable.save_binary(path) writes all tables to a single .ptbl file. Uses struct.pack for each table.
PtTable.load_binary(path) reads .ptbl file via memoryview. No pickle. Tables are read-only views into the buffer.
tasks.acceptance: PT.load_binary('tables.ptbl') produces same results as pickle

tasks.detail: Run save_binary to produce tables.ptbl in the repo. This file is the single source of truth for native code.
tasks.acceptance: tables.ptbl exists, ~56 MB, verified against pickle

phases.name: C Header — Opaque API Definition
phases.description: Define the minimal external interface. Everything else is hidden behind opaque pointers.

tasks.detail: typedef struct GeoField GeoField; typedef struct GeoResult GeoResult; — no internals exposed.
GeoField* geofield_init(const char* table_path); void geofield_destroy(GeoField*); — load tables, return opaque handle.
int32_t geofield_P(GeoField*, int32_t x, int32_t y); int32_t geofield_S(...); int32_t geofield_D(...); int32_t geofield_p_from_sd(...); int32_t geofield_proximity(...);
GeoResult* geofield_matmul(GeoField*, const int32_t* A, const int32_t* B, int m, int k, int n); — returns result matrix.
GeoResult* geofield_attention(GeoField*, const int32_t* tokens, int n_tokens, int window); — tokens as [id, S, D, P] flat array.
const int32_t* geofield_result_data(GeoResult*); int geofield_result_rows(GeoResult*); int geofield_result_cols(GeoResult*); void geofield_result_free(GeoResult*);
const char* geofield_last_error(GeoField*); — thread-local error string. No exceptions.

phases.name: Rust Implementation — Core Engine
phases.description: Implement the opaque API in Rust. Tables loaded via memmap. Hot paths are pure integer.

tasks.detail: Cargo.toml with memmap2, libc dependencies. #[no_mangle] pub extern "C" functions for C ABI.
Use memmap2 to load .ptbl file. Create typed views: P_table: &[i32], SP_table: &[i32], prox_table: &[i32]. All read-only.
pub fn p_from_sd(&self, s: i32, d: i32) -> i32 { self.SP[s * stride + (d + offset)] }. All functions are #[inline].
tasks.acceptance: All lookup functions match Python results

tasks.task: Implement matmul.rs — triple loop with lookup
tasks.detail: for i in 0..m { for p in 0..k { let a = A[i*k+p]; for j in 0..n { C[i*n+j] += product(a, B[p*n+j]); } } }. Use product() with gcd-scaling fallback.

tasks.task: Implement attention.rs — hashgrid with int weights
tasks.detail: HashGrid with Vec-based buckets. proximity lookup. int accumulation. PT.isqrt via integer sqrt crate.
tasks.acceptance: Results match Python hashgrid for 1000 tokens

tasks.detail: #[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn geofield_init(...) -> *mut GeoField. Opaque pointer pattern. Thread-safe (no mutable globals).
cargo test: verify all lookup functions, matmul, attention match expected values.

phases.name: Rust — SIMD Optimization (optional)
phases.description: Add SIMD vectorization for matmul inner loop using std::simd or packed_simd.

tasks.detail: Process 4 or 8 j-values in parallel using SIMD gather + multiply + horizontal add.

phases.name: Python Bindings — Opaque Wrapper
phases.description: Replace direct Python imports with CFFI/ctypes bindings to the native library. Python sees only the opaque API.

tasks.detail: Use cffi to load geofield.so/.dll. Wrap all C functions in Python classes.
Class NativePtTable that delegates P(), S(), D(), p_from_sd(), etc. to native library. Same API as PtTable.
def matmul(A, B): calls geofield_matmul via CFFI, returns Python list of lists.
def attention(tokens, window): calls geofield_attention via CFFI.
If native library not found, fall back to pure Python PtTable. Graceful degradation.

phases.name: Build System — Cross-Platform
phases.description: Automated build for Linux, Windows, macOS. Produce .so, .dll, .dylib.

tasks.detail: cargo build --release --lib. Copy .so/.dll to src/. Output: libgeofield.so or geofield.dll.
Option to embed tables.ptbl as a data segment in the binary (rust-embed or include_bytes!). Single-file distribution.
cargo build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, etc. For Raspberry Pi: armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf.

phases.name: Verification — Python = Native
phases.description: Comprehensive cross-verification that native library produces identical results to Python.

tasks.detail: Test 10000 random (x,y) pairs: PT.P(x,y) == native.P(x,y), PT.p_from_sd(s,d) == native.p_from_sd(s,d), etc.
Test 16x16, 32x32, 64x64: Python matmul == native matmul for all elements.
Test 100, 500, 1000 tokens: Python attention == native attention for all outputs.
Compare Python vs Rust speed for matmul and attention. Report speedup factor.

phases.name: Distribution — Opaque Package
phases.description: Create a distributable package that hides all internals. Users see only the opaque API.

tasks.detail: dist/geofield/ with __init__.py that imports from geofield_native. Pre-built .so/.dll included.
Only expose: GeoField.init(), GeoField.P(), GeoField.matmul(), GeoField.attention(). Everything else is private.
README shows how to use the API. No mention of tables, lookup, S/D/P internals. 'It just works.'
UNLICENSE or CC0. 'Do whatever you want.' No GPU, no Nvidia, no proprietary dependencies.

memory_layout.tables: Read-only, memory-mapped from .ptbl file or embedded in binary. Each process gets its own mmap — no contention.
memory_layout.hot_path: CPU registers + L1 cache. Tables accessed randomly but fit in L3 cache (56 MB).
memory_layout.mutable_state: HashGrid buckets, result matrices — allocated per call, freed after.
memory_layout.thread_safety: GeoField is immutable after init. Thread-safe. Multiple threads can call matmul/attention concurrently.

option_a_embedded.description: Tables embedded in binary as data segment
option_a_embedded.cons: Large binary, can't update tables without recompiling

option_a_external.pros: Small binary, tables can be updated independently

option_c_shared.description: Tables in shared memory (POSIX shm or mmap file)
option_c_shared.pros: Multiple processes share one copy of tables in RAM

binary_options.recommended: option_a_external for development, option_a_embedded for distribution

opaque_interface.philosophy: Users see a magic box that does geometric math. They don't need to know HOW. The box is fast, correct, and free.

dependencies: Phase 1 must complete before Phase 3 (native code needs .ptbl format)
Phase 2 must complete before Phase 3 (C API defines what to implement)
Phase 3 must complete before Phase 4 (Python bindings need native lib)
Phase 4 must complete before Phase 6 (verification needs both)
Phase 5 can run in parallel with Phase 3-4
risk_mitigation: Memory: 56 MB tables fit in L3 cache of modern CPUs (64-128 MB L3). No RAM bottleneck.
Portability: .ptbl format is platform-independent (little-endian int32). Works on any architecture.
Fallback: Pure Python always available if native build fails.
Threading: GeoField is immutable — thread-safe by design. No locks needed.
SIMD: Optional optimization. Core works without it.
